title: Writing practice: Penguins, Erasers and Ice Cubes
description: Eight short writing tasks: compare two birds, argue about a better buy, explain ice data, defend a town plan, explain classroom routines, tell a picture story, explain perimeter, and explain a late project.

stimuli.title: Fact table: Two birds that cannot fly
stimuli.caption: Facts about emperor penguins and ostriches.
rows: Antarctica, on ice and in the cold ocean
Africa, in grasslands and dry lands

stimuli.title: Price table: Erasers
stimuli.caption: Two packs of erasers at the school store. All erasers in both packs are the same size.

stimuli.title: Data table: Ice cubes in water
stimuli.caption: Three ice cubes of the same size were each put in a cup with the same amount of water. The table shows the water temperature and how long each ice cube took to melt completely. Heat moves from warmer things to colder things.

stimuli.title: Town plans for the empty lot on Cedar Street
stimuli.caption: Two plans for one empty lot. A total of 170 residents voted.
columns: What the plan gives the town
rows: 40 garden plots and a shaded place to sit

stimuli.title: Scenario: Routine chart for a substitute
paragraphs: Ms. Alvarez will be away tomorrow, so a substitute teacher will teach your class. Here is your class routine chart.
Arrival: hang backpacks on the hooks, put homework in the blue basket, and move your name card from “Home” to “Here.”
Bathroom: hold up two fingers, take the hall pass, and bring it back.
Dismissal: stack chairs on desks, pick up papers from the floor, and line up quietly by the door.

stimuli.title: Four pictures described in words
paragraphs: Picture 1: A boy named Omar stands behind his apartment building in the rain. He sees a small gray kitten under a bench. The kitten is shaking.
Picture 2: Omar wraps the kitten in a towel and carries it into the building.
Picture 3: Omar and his mother tape a sign to the front door. The sign says “Found kitten.”
Picture 4: A girl stands at the door and hugs the kitten. Omar is smiling.

stimuli.title: Math problem: Perimeter of a rectangle
paragraphs: Picture a rectangle. It has four sides. Two sides are 4 cm long. The other two sides are 2 cm long.
Perimeter is the distance around a shape.

stimuli.title: Scenario: The unfinished poster
paragraphs: Mr. Baptiste asked the class to finish a science poster about the Moon by Friday. On Tuesday you started your poster and wrote the title. On Wednesday you had a high fever and stayed home from school. On Thursday you came back, but your markers and pictures were still at home. Now it is Friday and your poster is not finished.
Mr. Baptiste asks, “Why isn’t your poster finished?”

items.stem: Compare emperor penguins and ostriches for a class book of animal facts. Write about one way they are the same and two ways they are different.

checklist: I wrote one way the birds are the same.
I wrote two ways the birds are different.
I used comparing words such as both, but, and however.
I used facts from the table.
exemplar: Task completion: includes one similarity (neither can fly) and two accurate differences from the table.
Organization: groups likenesses together and differences together.
Language: uses comparison words (both, but, while, however).
Accuracy: facts match the table.
Vocabulary: uses topic words such as Antarctica, grasslands, and squid.

support.clue: Read across each row. In which rows do the two birds have the same fact? In which rows are the facts different?
support.frame: Emperor penguins and ostriches are alike because both ______. They are different in two ways. First, penguins ______, but ostriches ______. Second, ______ while ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about two different animals. “Frogs and lizards are alike because both have four legs. They are different in two ways. First, frogs live near water, but many lizards live on dry land. Second, frogs have smooth skin while lizards have dry, scaly skin.” Notice the words that show how things are alike and different.

Compare the two birds in the same way.

facts: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica and eat fish and squid.
Emperor penguins are about 1 meter tall and cannot fly; they swim.
Ostriches live in Africa, eat plants, seeds, and some insects, are about 2 meters tall or more, and cannot fly; they run fast on land.

items.stem: Mr. Chen needs a lot of erasers for his class and wants to pay as little as possible for each eraser. Which pack is the better buy, Pack A or Pack B? Write your claim and prove it with math.

checklist: I wrote which pack is the better buy.
I showed the math for each pack.
I compared the packs in a fair way.
I used words such as because, since, and less than.
exemplar: Task completion: states a clear claim (Pack B) supported by the cost of one eraser.
Math accuracy: $3 ÷ 6 = $0.50 and $4 ÷ 10 = $0.40; compares correctly.
Reasoning: explains why comparing the cost of one eraser makes the comparison fair.
Vocabulary: uses terms such as divide, cost, each, and less than.

support.clue: Find a fair way to compare two packs that have different numbers of erasers.
support.frame: I think Pack ______ is the better buy. In Pack A, one eraser costs ______ because ______. In Pack B, ______. Since ______, ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different choice. “I think the library is the better place for our reading club. The library has 20 seats, and the classroom has 12 seats. Our club has 15 members. Since 20 is greater than 15, everyone can sit in the library. Since 12 is less than 15, three members would have no seat in the classroom.” Notice that the writer uses numbers to prove the claim.

Write your claim and proof in the same way.

facts: The prices in the table are invented for this practice.

items.stem: Explain what happened to the ice cubes in the three cups. Use numbers from the table and tell why the ice melted faster in some cups.

checklist: I used numbers from the table.
I told which ice cube melted fastest and which melted slowest.
I explained why the temperature changed how fast the ice melted.
I used science words such as heat, temperature, and melt.
exemplar: Task completion: describes the pattern (warmer water, faster melting) with data from at least two rows.
Reasoning: explains that heat moves from the warmer water to the colder ice.
Cohesion: uses connectors such as because, so, and as a result.
Vocabulary: uses terms such as temperature, heat, melt, and compare.
Accuracy: numbers match the table.

support.clue: Look at how the temperature changes from row to row and what happens to the number of minutes.
support.frame: The ice melted fastest in the ______ water, which took ______ minutes. It melted slowest in the ______ water, which took ______ minutes. This happened because ______. As a result, ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different topic. “The walkers on the flat path took 12 minutes. The walkers on the hill path took 20 minutes. This happened because climbing a hill takes more effort, so people walk more slowly. As a result, the walkers on the flat path arrived first.” Notice that the writer uses numbers and then gives a reason.

Explain the ice cubes in the same way.

facts: Heat moves from warmer things to colder things.
Warmer water gives heat to ice faster, so the ice melts sooner.
The temperatures and times in the table are invented for this practice.

items.stem: Write a letter to the town council. Say which plan the council should choose for the empty lot, and defend your choice with evidence from the table. Answer one reason someone might choose the other plan.

checklist: I used a greeting and a closing.
I wrote which plan I choose.
I used at least two pieces of evidence from the table.
I answered a reason for the other plan.
I used polite, formal language.
exemplar: Task completion: states a clear choice and supports it with two or more details from the table (cost, votes, what each plan gives). Either plan can be defended with evidence.
Counterargument: recognizes a real strength of the other plan (the garden costs $18,000 less; the parking lot got more votes) and responds to it.
Organization: opening request, evidence, response to the other side, and closing.
Language: formal tone and connectors such as in addition, however, and for these reasons.
Reasoning: explains why the evidence matters for the town.

support.clue: Compare the cost, the benefit, and the votes for each plan. Think about who will use each plan.
support.frame: Dear Town Council, I am writing to ask you to choose the ______. First, ______. In addition, ______. Some people may want the ______ because ______. However, ______. For these reasons, ______. Sincerely, ______
support.model:
Mentor example about a different town choice. “Dear Council, I am writing to ask you to build the bike path. First, it costs $8,000, but the bus shelter costs $25,000. In addition, 90 residents voted for the path. Some people may want the shelter because it keeps riders dry. However, the path costs much less and more residents want it. Sincerely, Amara.” Notice how the writer answers the other side.

Write your letter in the same way.

facts: The garden costs less than the parking lot.
The cost and vote numbers in the table are invented for this practice.
The parking lot got more votes than the garden (92 compared with 78).

items.stem: Write a note to the substitute teacher. Tell about the three routines so the substitute knows what students do and in what order.

checklist: I wrote about all three routines.
I told the steps in each routine in order.
I used words such as first, next, then, and finally.
I used polite language for a note to an adult.
exemplar: Task completion: covers arrival, bathroom, and dismissal with the main steps for each.
Organization: one routine at a time, steps in order.
Language: uses sequence words and commands or statements (students hang, you should).
Audience: respectful tone suited to a note to a teacher.
Clarity: the substitute could follow the routines.

support.clue: Find the three headings on the chart. Under each heading, notice the actions and the order they happen in.
support.frame: Dear Substitute Teacher, here is how our class works. At arrival, students ______. Then ______. For the bathroom, a student ______. At dismissal, first ______. Finally, ______. Thank you for ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different routine. “Dear Substitute Teacher, here is how we do lunch. First, students wash their hands. Next, they line up in two rows by the door. Then they walk quietly to the cafeteria. Finally, they throw away trash and return to the room. Thank you for helping us.” Notice how the sequence words guide the reader.

Write about your three routines in the same way.

items.stem: Use the four pictures to write a story. Tell what happened in each picture and how Omar felt.

checklist: I wrote about all four pictures in order.
I told how Omar felt at least once.
I used time words such as first, then, and in the end.
I used past-tense verbs.
exemplar: Task completion: includes the key event from each of the four pictures in the right order.
Development: adds at least one feeling or detail (for example, Omar worried or happy).
Organization: clear beginning, middle, and end with time words.
Language: past-tense verbs are used consistently.
Cohesion: pronouns and linking words connect the events.

support.clue: Look at what changes from picture to picture. What problem does Omar see, and what does he do about it?
support.frame: One rainy day, Omar saw ______. At first, he felt ______. Then he ______. After that, he and his mother ______. In the end, ______. Omar felt ______ because ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different story. “One windy day, Mei saw a paper boat stuck in a puddle. At first, she felt curious. Then she pulled it out with a stick. After that, she dried it on the step. In the end, she floated it in a bigger puddle. Mei felt happy because the boat sailed away.” Notice the time words and the feelings.

Tell your story about the pictures in the same way.

items.stem: Explain how to find the perimeter of the rectangle. Tell each step and give the perimeter.

checklist: I told what perimeter means.
I used all four side lengths.
I told what I did with the numbers.
I wrote the perimeter with cm.
exemplar: Task completion: states that perimeter is the distance around, uses all four sides, and gives 12 cm.
Math accuracy: 4 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 12.
Organization: steps are in order with first, then.
Vocabulary: uses perimeter, side, length, and add.

support.clue: Perimeter goes all the way around. Count how many sides the rectangle has and write each length.
support.frame: The perimeter is the distance ______ the shape. First, I wrote the lengths of the ______ sides: ______. Then I ______ them. The perimeter is ______ cm.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different shape. “A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm. The perimeter is the distance around the shape. First, I wrote the three sides: 3, 4, and 6. Then I added them. 3 + 4 + 6 = 13. The perimeter is 13 cm.” Notice that the writer uses every side.

Explain your rectangle in the same way.

facts: Perimeter is the distance around a shape.

items.stem: Write a note to Mr. Baptiste. Explain why the poster is not finished and what you will do next to finish it.

checklist: I explained what happened in order.
I used because or so to show the reasons.
I told what I will do next and when.
I used polite and respectful language.
I ended with thanks.
exemplar: Task completion: explains the causes (fever, absence, materials at home) and states a next step with a plan.
Organization: events in time order, then the plan.
Language: complex sentences with because, so, and since; a polite tone for a teacher.
Cohesion: time and cause connectors link the days to the result.
Clarity: Mr. Baptiste could understand what happened and what will happen next.

support.clue: Make a list of what happened on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Which events caused the poster to be unfinished?
support.frame: Dear Mr. Baptiste, I am sorry that my poster is not finished. On Tuesday, I ______. However, on Wednesday I ______ because ______. As a result, ______. On Thursday, ______. Because of this, ______. Next, I will ______. Thank you for ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different problem. “Dear Ms. Osei, I am sorry that my book report is late. On Monday, I finished reading the book. However, on Tuesday my family traveled to see my grandmother, so I could not write. As a result, I only wrote the first paragraph. Next, I will write the rest tonight and give it to you tomorrow. Thank you for understanding.” Notice how each reason is joined to a result.

Write your note in the same way.
